getting-started.title: Getting Started & Initial Setup
getting-started.subtitle: Complete guide for deploying your clinic in the OdontoFlow ecosystem, ensuring full compliance from day one.

sections.p: First, go to 'Settings > Clinic' and fill out basic information like name, address, and phone. This is important because the system uses this to create the beautiful header on all prescriptions and receipts handed to your patients.

In the 'Team' tab, invite the people who work with you. It's very practical: a receptionist will only see the calendar and front desk, while a dentist gets direct access to their patients' charts. Everyone has their designated workspace without confusion.

Dentists just need to open their profile and add their professional license number and set up their Digital Certificate. Once done, they will never need to stamp paper again—they can sign prescriptions directly in the system.

scheduling.title: Appointment Management & Reception Flow
scheduling.subtitle: Automate patient reception and traffic using smart triage.

sections.p: Using the calendar is just like on your phone. You pick a day, find a free slot, and book the patient. The appointment block changes color on its own to let you know if the patient confirmed, arrived, or is currently in the chair.
When the patient walks in, reception clicks 'Check-in'. Instantly, the dentist's computer notifies them that their 2 PM patient is here. It's the end of the intercom ringing constantly.

If your clinic takes blood pressure or asks about the visit reason before the dentist sees them, the Triage tab handles this. You jot it down quickly, and the dentist reads it before the patient even sits in the chair.

health-records.title: Electronic Health Records & Interoperability
health-records.subtitle: The clinical heart of OdontoFlow: diagnostic precision with full legal validity.

sections.p: The dentist's main screen features a full drawing of the patient's mouth. If a filling is needed, just click the tooth and mark it. The system understands what was done and automatically adds it to the patient's history.

When writing down how the visit went, the dentist has free space to type. If a prescription or work note is needed, the system has ready-made templates. Just fill in the days off and hit print or send via WhatsApp.

At the end of the visit, the system asks for the dentist's password (digital signature). This 'locks' the chart for that day, ensuring no one alters the work and giving it full validity, just like a legally notarized document.

billing.title: Financial Management, Inventory & Business Intelligence
billing.subtitle: Connect clinical decisions to cash flow without double data entry.

sections.p: Remember that drawing the dentist made on the tooth? Reception can turn it into a budget with one click. If the patient approves, the system creates the bill to be paid by card, and the money enters the cash flow.

When a box of gloves arrives, you enter the invoice into the system. OdontoFlow stores the gloves in your virtual cabinet and reminds you in the finance tab that you have a bill to pay the supplier next week.

On the main screen (Dashboard), the manager gets easy-to-read charts. You can see instantly if the clinic made a profit this month, how many new patients walked in, and which dentist saw the most people. Everything is simplified to help the clinic grow.

system-flowchart.subtitle: Discover how OdontoFlow modules connect end-to-end.

sections.p: It all starts when the patient reaches out. The receptionist schedules the appointment and gives them a 'Check-in' on the day of the visit. The best part is there's no double entry: the name typed at the front desk is exactly what shows up on the dentist's chart and the payment receipt.

While waiting, the team can note if the patient is in severe pain or check their blood pressure. The system is smart: if the patient reports an urgent issue, their name is highlighted on the dentist's screen to prioritize care.

Inside, the dentist opens the Visual Odontogram and simply clicks on the teeth to indicate what needs to be done. When finished, they write their notes, generate a prescription, and digitally sign it with their password. No more paper folders passing around!

When it's time to leave, the treatment plan drawn by the dentist appears at the reception computer with the final prices. Once paid, the clinic owner can instantly see the money hitting the cash flow on their phone's dashboard.
